questions.prompt: When approaching a Yield sign, you must:
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down and be ready to stop. Give the right-of-way to traffic that does not face the sign and to all pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

choices.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic not facing the sign and all pedestrians in the intersection
Always sound the horn to warn other traffic within the intersection
Expect all other vehicles to yield the right-of-way to you
Come to a stop and proceed after looking to the right and left

questions.prompt: When encountering a funeral procession that is crossing an intersection:
questions.explanation: Let a funeral procession pass through the intersection as a group. Yield and don't cut through the line of vehicles. Key words: "do not break through".

choices.text: Sound the horn before proceeding
Proceed through the funeral procession only when there is sufficient space between vehicles
Yield the right-of-way and do not break through the procession
Flash the high beam headlights before proceeding

questions.prompt: A vehicle exiting a parking lot onto a roadway:
questions.explanation: When leaving a parking lot, alley or driveway, come to a complete stop before the sidewalk area, then yield to pedestrians and to traffic on the road.

choices.text: Must stop only if there is a Stop sign
Is not required to stop
Must stop before crossing the sidewalk only if there are pedestrians present
Must come to a complete stop

questions.prompt: In an urban area, when a pedestrian is standing at a crosswalk with their arm raised at approximately right angles to their body and pointing to the opposite curb, what does this mean?
questions.explanation: A pedestrian pointing across the road with an outstretched arm is signalling that they want to cross. Drivers must stop and yield. Key words: "urban area", "must stop and yield".

choices.text: Drivers must stop and yield to the pedestrian
The pedestrian is visually impaired and needs assistance to cross the road
Drivers do not have to yield to the pedestrian until they step off the curb
Drivers should reduce speed to 30 km/h and be cautious when passing the pedestrian

questions.prompt: When facing a Merge sign a driver should:
questions.explanation: A merge sign means two lanes of traffic are joining. Use the acceleration lane to match highway speed, find a gap, and blend in smoothly. Don't stop unless you have to.

choices.text: Stop at the entrance to the other highway and wait until a gap in traffic occurs before proceeding
Watch for a gap in traffic on the highway they are entering, adjust to highway speed in the acceleration lane and blend in smoothly
Stop and yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the highway
Reduce speed and proceed with caution

questions.prompt: When two vehicles approach an uncontrolled "T" intersection at right angles to each other at approximately the same time:
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, including a "T" intersection, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right. Key words: "left".

choices.text: The vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way
The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way
The vehicle going straight through always has the right-of-way
Both vehicles must stop

questions.prompt: A driver entering a traffic circle:
questions.explanation: Vehicles already in a traffic circle have the right-of-way. When entering, yield to them and wait for a safe gap. Key words: "entering".

choices.text: Must yield to traffic on the right
Must yield to vehicles in the traffic circle
Has the right-of-way
